topicName: Metrics and Tracking: Velocity, Burn-down, and Flow Metrics
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Metrics and Tracking: Velocity, Burn-down, and Flow Metrics in Scrum"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Effective tracking in Scrum allows teams to measure their progress, forecast future capacity, and continuously improve their delivery processes. Relying solely on intuition is insufficient; empirical data must guide Scrum teams."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Velocity"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Velocity is a measure of the amount of value (usually expressed in story points or user stories) a Scrum Team delivers during a single Sprint. It is calculated at the end of the Sprint by summing the estimation points of all completed and fully accepted Product Backlog items."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Purpose: Helps the team forecast how much work they can take on in future Sprints during Sprint Planning."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Calculation: Total Story Points of Completed Items = Velocity for Sprint X."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Anti-pattern: Using velocity as a performance metric to compare different teams. Velocity is strictly an internal forecasting metric."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Sprint Burn-down Charts"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"A Sprint Burn-down chart is a graphical representation of work left to do versus time. The horizontal axis represents days in the Sprint, and the vertical axis represents remaining effort (usually in hours or story points)."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Ideal Progress Line: A straight diagonal line representing the expected rate at which work should be completed."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Actual Progress Line: Tracks the real-time remaining work, fluctuating based on daily updates."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"Day 1: 50 pts | Day 3: 40 pts | Day 5: 25 pts | Day 10 (End): 0 pts"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Flow Metrics (Kanban and Scrum Integration)"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"While velocity and burn-down are traditional Scrum metrics, Flow Metrics provide deeper operational insights into how work moves through the workflow."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"WIP (Work in Progress): The total number of items currently in progress but not yet completed."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Cycle Time: The amount of time it takes for a work item to travel from the start of development to completion."},{"order":17,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Throughput: The number of items completed per unit of time (e.g., items per week)."},{"order":18,"type":"heading","text":"Summary"},{"order":19,"type":"paragraph","text":"By combining Velocity for Sprint-level planning, Burn-downs for daily tracking, and Flow Metrics for operational efficiency, Scrum teams can achieve transparency, inspect accurately, and adapt their processes effectively."}]
